blocks.prompt: 6. Find the equation of the circle passing through the point \((-3, -4)\) and touching the line \(3x - y - 1 = 0\) at the point \((1, 2)\).
blocks.explanation:
Two points on the circle, and the tangent at one of them: Case 3 (Example 7).
We need the equation.
Plan: two point-equations, plus "the centre lies on the normal at \((1, 2)\)"; solve for \(g, f, c\).
steps:
Given: the circle passes through \((-3, -4)\) and touches \(3x - y - 1 = 0\) at \((1, 2)\).
To find: the equation of the circle.
Method: Case 3. The point of contact \((1, 2)\) is on the circle, and the radius to it is perpendicular to the tangent, so the centre lies on the normal at \((1, 2)\).

Through \((1, 2)\)
\[1 + 4 + 2g + 4f + c = 0\]
\[2g + 4f + c + 5 = 0 \quad (1)\]
Why: The point of contact lies on the circle \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\).

Through \((-3, -4)\)
\[9 + 16 - 6g - 8f + c = 0\]
\[-6g - 8f + c + 25 = 0 \quad (2)\]
Why: The second point lies on the circle.

The normal at \((1, 2)\)
\[3x - y - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow m = 3\]
\[\text{normal slope} = -\tfrac{1}{3}\]
\[y - 2 = -\tfrac{1}{3}(x - 1)\]
\[x + 3y - 7 = 0\]
Why: Perpendicular slopes multiply to \(-1\).

Centre on the normal
\[(-g) + 3(-f) - 7 = 0\]
\[g + 3f = -7 \quad (3)\]
Why: The centre \((-g, -f)\) satisfies the normal's equation.

Solve (3) and (4)
\[(4) - (3):\ g = 12\]
\[12 + 3f = -7,\quad f = -\tfrac{19}{3}\]
Why: Subtracting removes \(3f\).

The equation
\[x^2 + y^2 + 24x - \tfrac{38}{3}y - \tfrac{11}{3} = 0\]
\[3x^2 + 3y^2 + 72x - 38y - 11 = 0\]
Why: Put \(g, f, c\) in the general form; multiply by 3.

Check (tangency)
\[\text{centre} = \left(-12, \tfrac{19}{3}\right),\ r^2 = \tfrac{1690}{9}\]
\[\text{distance} = \dfrac{|-36 - \frac{19}{3} - 1|}{\sqrt{10}}\]
\[= \dfrac{130}{3\sqrt{10}} = \dfrac{13\sqrt{10}}{3} = r \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(r^2 = 144 + \frac{361}{9} + \frac{11}{3} = \frac{1690}{9}\), so \(r = \frac{13\sqrt{10}}{3}\); the distance from the centre to the line equals the radius, so the line really touches the circle.
